questions.question: Which organ in the human body purifies blood?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter and purify blood.

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet.

questions.question: The chemical symbol for gold is:
questions.explanation: Gold’s symbol Au comes from Latin "aurum".

questions.question: How many members can the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha for expertise in arts, science, etc.

questions.question: GST was implemented in India on:
questions.explanation: GST came into effect on 1 July 2017.

questions.question: The SI unit of force is:
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.question: The gas responsible for the greenhouse effect is mainly:
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is the main greenhouse gas.

questions.question: The hardest natural substance known is:
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest known natural substance.

questions.question: The currency of the United States is the:
questions.explanation: The US currency is the Dollar.

questions.question: Water boils at what temperature at sea level?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100°C at standard sea-level pressure.

questions.question: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi became PM in 1966.

questions.question: Which part of the plant conducts photosynthesis using the green pigment?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that captures light energy.

questions.question: The concept of "Directive Principles of State Policy" was borrowed from which country?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

questions.question: How many players are there in a kabaddi team on the court?
questions.explanation: A kabaddi team has 7 players on the court.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which city?
questions.explanation: It occurred at Amritsar on 13 April 1919.

questions.question: The powerhouse of the cell is the:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce energy (ATP), so they are the cell’s powerhouse.

questions.question: Which blood group is known as the universal donor?
questions.explanation: O-negative is the universal donor blood group.

questions.question: Emperor Ashoka belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Ashoka was a Mauryan emperor.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: The INC was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume.

questions.question: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by the:
questions.explanation: The CAG is appointed by the President of India.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties are in Part IVA (Article 51A), added by the 42nd Amendment.

questions.question: Who composed the song "Vande Mataram"?
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote "Vande Mataram".

questions.question: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution was inspired by the Constitution of:
questions.explanation: The idea of a Preamble was borrowed from the US Constitution.

questions.question: Which disease is caused by a deficiency of iodine?
questions.explanation: Iodine deficiency causes goitre.

questions.question: Which is the southernmost point of mainland India?
questions.explanation: Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India (Indira Point is the southernmost of Indian territory).

questions.question: Which line divides the Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres?
questions.explanation: The Equator divides the Earth into two hemispheres.

questions.question: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver is the largest gland in the human body.

questions.question: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
questions.explanation: Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir is the largest freshwater lake in India.

questions.question: The "Sun Temple" at Konark is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Konark Sun Temple is in Odisha.

questions.question: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as per the Constitution is:
questions.explanation: The Constitution permits a maximum of 550 elected members in the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is required for blood clotting.

questions.question: The Simon Commission came to India in:
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission arrived in 1928 and was widely boycotted.

questions.question: The Rajya Sabha has a maximum strength of:
questions.explanation: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members.

questions.question: Which river is the longest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile is generally regarded as the longest river in the world.

questions.question: Light travels fastest in:
questions.explanation: Light travels fastest in a vacuum (~3×10⁸ m/s).

questions.question: The Indus Valley Civilisation is also known as the:
questions.explanation: It is called the Harappan Civilisation after Harappa, its first excavated site.

questions.question: Which amendment is known as the "Mini Constitution"?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) is called the "Mini Constitution" for its sweeping changes.

questions.question: The headquarters of the United Nations is in:
questions.explanation: The UN headquarters is in New York City.

questions.question: The process by which plants lose water through leaves is called:
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves.

questions.question: The "Right to Education" was made a fundamental right by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 21A — Right to Education.

questions.question: Which tax was subsumed under GST?
questions.explanation: Service Tax (among others) was subsumed under GST.

questions.question: The Sundarbans delta is formed by which rivers?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans is formed by the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta.

questions.question: The currency of the United Kingdom is the:
questions.explanation: The UK uses the Pound Sterling.

questions.question: Which river is known as the "Sorrow of Bihar"?
questions.explanation: The Kosi river is called the "Sorrow of Bihar" due to flooding.

questions.question: The national flower of India is the:
questions.explanation: The lotus is India’s national flower.

questions.question: The national bird of India is the:
questions.explanation: The Indian peacock is the national bird.

questions.question: The Olympic Games are held once every how many years?
questions.explanation: The Summer Olympics are held every 4 years.

questions.question: If today is Monday, what day will it be after 36 days?
questions.explanation: 36 mod 7 = 1; Monday + 1 = Tuesday.

questions.question: Which letter is 3rd to the right of the 4th letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: 4th letter = D; 4 + 3 = 7th letter = G.

questions.question: Find the odd pair: (4, 63), (9, 729), (5, 125), (6, 216)
questions.explanation: In each correct pair the second number is the cube of the first. 4³ = 64, not 63.

questions.question: In a row of 42 students, Ravi is 11th from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.explanation: Position from right = 42 − 11 + 1 = 32.

questions.question: Find the next term: 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, ?
questions.explanation: These are perfect squares 4²…8². Next is 9² = 81.

questions.question: Find the next term: 1, 3, 8, 16, 27, ?
questions.explanation: Differences increase by 3 each step; next difference is 14, so 27 + 14 = 41.

questions.question: If STAR is coded as WXEV, how is CAT coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 4. Applying the same to CAT gives GEX.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 3:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark = 30°. At 3:00 the angle is 3 × 30° = 90°.
The relation is squaring: 11² = 121, so 9² = 81.

questions.question: A person walks 6 km East and then 8 km North. What is the shortest distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Shortest distance = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km.

questions.question: If + means ×, and × means −, then evaluate: 11 + 3 × 3.
questions.explanation: Replace symbols: 11 × 3 − 3 = 33 − 3 = 30.

questions.question: Find the next term: 5, 15, 45, 135, ?
questions.explanation: Each term follows ×3: 135 × 3 = 405.

questions.question: Complete the series: A, D, G, J, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter advances by 3 places, so the next is M.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 3, 20, 11, 13
questions.explanation: 3, 11, 13 are prime numbers; 20 is a composite number.

questions.question: Which letter is 3rd from the right end of the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: The 3rd letter from the right is the 24th from the left = X.
The relation is cubing: 5³ = 125, so 4³ = 64.

questions.question: If today is Tuesday, what day will it be after 42 days?
questions.explanation: 42 mod 7 = 0; Tuesday + 0 = Tuesday.

questions.question: Which letter is 8th to the right of the 6th letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: 6th letter = F; 6 + 8 = 14th letter = N.

questions.question: Find the odd pair: (9, 729), (8, 516), (6, 216), (2, 8)
questions.explanation: In each correct pair the second number is the cube of the first. 8³ = 512, not 516.

questions.question: In a row of 29 students, Ravi is 11th from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.explanation: Position from right = 29 − 11 + 1 = 19.

questions.question: Find the next term: 6, 8, 12, 18, 26, ?
questions.explanation: Differences increase by 2 each step; next difference is 10, so 26 + 10 = 36.

questions.question: Find the next term: 5, 8, 14, 23, 35, ?
questions.explanation: Differences increase by 3 each step; next difference is 15, so 35 + 15 = 50.

questions.question: If TREE is coded as WUHH, how is BIRD coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 3. Applying the same to BIRD gives ELUG.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 6:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark = 30°. At 6:00 the angle is 6 × 30° = 180°.
The relation is squaring: 8² = 64, so 11² = 121.

questions.question: What is 20% of 60?
Find the simple interest on ₹2000 at 12% per annum for 2 years.
Find the compound interest on ₹5000 at 5% per annum for 2 years.
An article costing ₹700 is sold for ₹840. Find the profit percentage.
An article costing ₹360 is sold at a 20% profit. Find the selling price.
Find the average of the first five multiples of 5.
questions.explanation: Multiples: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. Sum = 75. Average = 75/5 = 15.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4 and their sum is 35. Find the larger number.
questions.explanation: Total parts = 7. Each part = 35/7 = 5. Larger = 4 × 5 = 20.

questions.question: A train 150 m long crosses a pole in 9 seconds. Find its speed in km/h.
A can do a work in 12 days and B in 6 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.explanation: Combined one-day work = 1/12 + 1/6 = 18/72. Time = 72/18 = 4 days.

questions.question: Find the area of a circle with radius 21 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
Find the value of √900.
After a 20% discount, an item costs ₹560. Find its marked price.
Find 50% of 10% of 600.
Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 9 and their difference is 20. Find the smaller number.
questions.explanation: Difference = 4 parts = 20, so each part = 5. Smaller = 5 × 5 = 25.

questions.question: A boat travels 26 km downstream in 2 hours. If the speed of the stream is 1 km/h, find the speed of the boat in still water.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 26/2 = 13 km/h = boat + stream. Boat = 13 − 1 = 12 km/h.
